title: API 653 Training in Houston: Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: Online API 653 exam prep for Houston tank inspectors: Ship Channel terminals, breakout tanks, SPCC, settlement on Gulf Coast soils and instructor Q&A.
h1: API 653 Training in Houston: Self-Paced Exam Prep for Terminal, Refinery and Pipeline Tank Inspectors
html:
API 653 exam prep for Houston tank inspectors

Kinder Morgan's Pasadena and Galena Park terminals alone list 381 tanks between them, and they are only two of the storage sites on the channel between downtown Houston and Galveston Bay. Refinery tank farms, independent terminals, chemical storage and the tankage that feeds long-distance pipelines all need inspectors who can judge a shell course, a floor and a foundation against API Std 653. This page explains how candidates in Pasadena, Galena Park, Deer Park, Channelview, Baytown, Seabrook and Texas City prepare for the API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector examination with the Atlantis course.

The course is self-paced online study with an instructor who answers your questions, built around the Body of Knowledge for your exam window. There is no Atlantis classroom in Houston. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility under Annex D of API 653, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification; Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and each candidate applies to API individually.

Houston's tank terminals, in their own figures

The operators' published terminal data gives a sense of the inspection load. The figures below come from each company's own terminal page or fact sheet, as published when this page was written.

Refinery tank farms at Baytown, Deer Park, Pasadena, Texas City and the other plants in EIA's 2026 refinery list hold crude, intermediates and finished products on top of that, and the chemical plants keep their own feed and product tanks. Between them, these sites employ owner-user tank inspectors, contract API 653 inspectors and the NDT crews who scan floors and measure shells for them.

The rules that put an API 653 inspector on a Houston tank

API 653 is an industry standard, so the reason a particular tank is inspected to it usually sits in a federal rule or the owner's own programme. The table summarises the requirements a Houston candidate meets most often.

Requirements that point Houston tanks to API 653
RuleWhere it appliesWhat it asks of the owner
EPA SPCC, 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6)Oil storage at facilities covered by the Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure ruleTest or inspect each aboveground container for integrity on a regular schedule and after material repairs, following industry standards; inspect supports and foundations; keep comparison records
PHMSA, 49 CFR 195.432(b)Atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks on hazardous liquid pipelinesInspect the physical integrity of in-service tanks according to API Std 653, without using its risk-based procedures to set the internal interval
PHMSA, 49 CFR 195.432(c)Pressurised steel breakout tanks built to API Std 2510Inspect according to section 6 of API 510, which takes those tanks outside API 653
OSHA Process Safety ManagementStorage tanks that form part of a covered processInspect and test following recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices

EPA's integrity-testing fact sheet notes that API 653 is the standard typically used for field-erected tanks, while STI SP001 covers shop-fabricated and small field-erected tanks, and that once an owner cites API 653 in the SPCC plan, implementing its relevant portions becomes mandatory for that facility. The same fact sheet says testing and inspection records must be kept for three years and recommends keeping formal test reports for the life of the tank.

The state programme matters less than many newcomers expect. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality regulates many petroleum ASTs, but its rules in 30 TAC 334.123 exempt tanks located at petroleum refineries, petrochemical plants and bulk facilities, and tanks connected to pipelines regulated under federal or Texas pipeline safety law. Along the Ship Channel, that leaves many of the largest tanks to the federal rules and the owner's programme. The breakout tank row reflects the federal rule as it stands; PHMSA proposed in 2026 to allow API 653's risk-based procedure for those tanks within capped intervals, and no final rule had been issued when this page was written.

Ground, rain and chemicals: what Houston tanks ask of an inspector

Settlement on sinking ground

The Harris-Galveston Subsidence District, created by the Texas Legislature in 1975 to regulate groundwater withdrawal, records subsidence in the Houston region as early as 1908, with the highest historical rates near the coast. On soft coastal ground of that kind, settlement surveys are a routine part of tank inspection. The API 653 Body of Knowledge expects you to calculate edge settlement, bottom settlement near the shell and localised settlement remote from the shell under Annex B, and to work out the number of survey points a tank needs.

Floors, soil and cathodic protection

A high water table and wet soils make the underside of a tank floor a constant concern. Soil corrosion and microbiologically influenced corrosion are among the API RP 571 mechanisms on the 653 list, and API RP 651 on cathodic protection and RP 652 on bottom linings are both examined. In the field, that knowledge is used every time an MFL floor scan or UT prove-up has to be turned into a minimum remaining thickness and a next internal inspection date. The API RP 651 summary covers the cathodic protection side.

Ethanol, caustic and acid service

Kinder Morgan's terminal sheets list ethanol among the products at both Pasadena and Galena Park, undenatured ethanol included at Galena Park, and ethanol stress corrosion cracking is one of the listed RP 571 mechanisms. Chemical terminals store caustic and acids, which bring caustic stress corrosion cracking and sulfuric acid corrosion into play. Stainless steel tanks such as those at Odfjell's terminal raise their own questions about which construction standard applies, so read API 653's scope section carefully.

Heavy rain and floating roofs

Gulf Coast downpours load floating roofs and their drains hard. Roof, seal and drain condition is routine inspection work at Houston terminals, and you should know where API 653 deals with roofs and what the examination expects you to judge about them.

A Houston terminal example for the open-book half

Fill-height decisions are everyday work at a terminal and a regular exam theme. Take a hypothetical gasoline tank at a Pasadena terminal: 180 ft diameter, maximum liquid level 48 ft, specific gravity 0.75 for this example, unknown shell material and a joint efficiency of 1.0 on record. For unknown material, API 653 gives an allowable stress of 23,600 psi for the bottom two courses.

  1. Whole-course minimum thickness for the first course: tmin = 2.6 (H − 1) D G / (S E) = 2.6 × 47 × 180 × 0.75 / 23,600 = 0.699 in.
  2. The lowest average thickness found in the first course is 0.640 in., so the course cannot carry product to 48 ft.
  3. Maximum fill height at the measured thickness: H = S E t / (2.6 D G) + 1 = 23,600 × 0.640 / 351 + 1 = 44.0 ft.
  4. Before quoting that figure, subtract the metal you expect to lose before the next inspection, which lowers the safe fill height further.

The owner then chooses between a lower operating level, a repair or a reconstruction. Questions are built the same way: the formula is given, and the marks go to choosing the right one, the right stress value for the course and the right corrosion allowance. The API 653 shell minimum thickness guide and the API 653 tank inspection guide go further.

Routes into API 653 from Houston terminal and refinery jobs

Annex D of API 653 combines education with tank experience gained in the last ten years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency, from one year with an engineering or technology degree up to five or more years without formal education. The API 653 certification requirements page has the full scale.

  • MFL and UT technicians who scan floors and gauge shells at terminals already work beside API 653 inspectors and often see every report. ASNT SNT-TC-1A training in UT, MT, PT, VT and MFL is on the Houston NDT training page.
  • Tank construction and repair crews, including welders and foremen on shell and floor replacements, bring repair and reconstruction experience that counts on the two-year and high school routes alongside a year of inspection.
  • Terminal maintenance and operations staff know the tanks, mixers, roofs and drains intimately but need documented inspection time.
  • Coating and lining inspectors who work on tank bottoms find RP 652 familiar ground.
  • Engineers at terminal operators and refineries reach eligibility after one year of tank inspection activity with a bachelor's degree.

Studying API 653 around terminal schedules

Terminal inspection follows the tanks rather than a calendar. A tank comes out of service, is cleaned and opened, and for a few weeks everyone is busy with the internal inspection, repairs and hydrotest; then the pace drops until the next one. A self-paced course lets you study hard in the quiet periods and pause during an out-of-service job without falling behind a class.

Bring your own reports into your study. When a floor scan, a settlement survey or a repair plan you worked on does not seem to match what API 653 or API 650 says, send the question to the instructor. The answer comes from the code text, and working through a real case is often the quickest way to fix where a rule lives in the document for the open-book session.

Comparing your options in Houston

San Jacinto College and Lone Star College teach inspection technology over several terms, which suits people starting out but is not tied to the API 653 examination. Private training companies run in-person API prep on fixed dates for those who can leave work for it. Large terminal operators sometimes pair candidates with an experienced inspector, which builds judgement but rarely covers the whole Body of Knowledge. The Atlantis course sits between these: exam-focused, self-paced, with practice papers and an instructor to ask, and fees quoted on request.

Exam day and employer sponsorship

Once API approves your application, you book through Prometric, which lists test centres in and around Houston. The examination has 170 questions, 110 closed-book and 60 open-book, over a day of about 7.5 hours, with the API 653, API 650 and other listed documents provided as PDFs for the open-book session. Windows and deadlines are on the API exam schedule page.

Terminal operators, refiners and inspection contractors can enrol several tank inspection candidates together, alongside candidates for other API exams. Each candidate applies to API with their own experience record and studies at their own pace. Employers can help most by letting candidates see a tank through its whole out-of-service cycle before the exam.

faq.q: Do Houston terminals need API 653 inspectors, or is it optional?
faq.a: For many tanks it is effectively required. Pipeline operators must inspect atmospheric breakout tanks to API Std 653 under 49 CFR 195.432, and facilities covered by EPA's SPCC rule must inspect aboveground containers to an industry standard, which for large field-erected tanks is usually API 653. Owners then specify certified inspectors in their programmes and contracts. Check each employer's requirement before assuming a certificate covers a scope.

faq.q: Does the TCEQ inspect the big terminal tanks along the Ship Channel?
faq.a: Usually not under its petroleum storage tank programme. The rules in 30 TAC 334.123 exempt aboveground tanks at petroleum refineries, petrochemical plants and bulk facilities, and tanks connected to pipelines regulated under federal or Texas pipeline safety law. Those tanks are inspected under federal rules such as SPCC and PHMSA's breakout tank requirements, and under the owner's own mechanical integrity or tank programme.

faq.q: Are pressurised spheres and bullets covered by API 653?
faq.a: No. API 653 deals with atmospheric and low-pressure aboveground storage tanks. Pressurised storage, such as LPG spheres and bullets, is pressure vessel work. For pipeline breakout tanks built to API Std 2510, 49 CFR 195.432(c) requires inspection according to section 6 of API 510. If spheres are your daily work, the API 510 examination is the closer match.

faq.q: How does Houston's subsidence show up on the API 653 exam?
faq.a: Not by name, but through settlement. The Body of Knowledge expects you to calculate allowable edge settlement, bottom settlement near the shell and localised bottom settlement remote from the shell using Annex B, and to determine the number of survey points. Houston candidates who have read real settlement surveys on soft coastal ground usually find the figures and terms easier to follow.

faq.q: Can an MFL floor-scan technician in Houston qualify for API 653?
faq.a: Often, if the floor scanning and related work count as performing tank inspection activities as API 653 describes them and were done for an employer or contractor that qualifies as an authorized inspection agency. The years required depend on your education under Annex D. Keep a log of the tanks you scanned, the reports you contributed to and who reviewed them, because API verifies documented experience.

faq.q: Is ethanol stress corrosion cracking on the API 653 exam?
faq.a: Yes. Ethanol stress corrosion cracking is one of the API RP 571 mechanisms listed in the current API 653 Body of Knowledge, alongside soil corrosion, microbiologically influenced corrosion, caustic stress corrosion cracking, brittle fracture and others. Terminals that store fuel ethanol, as Kinder Morgan's Pasadena and Galena Park sites do, make it a practical topic as well as an examined one.

faq.q: Can a Galena Park or Pasadena terminal operator enrol several inspectors?
faq.a: Yes. Terminal operators, refiners and inspection contractors can enrol a group of API 653 candidates, and the group can include people preparing for API 510 or API 570. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate studies at their own pace with access to the instructor and applies to API individually. Tell us the number of candidates and the windows you are aiming for.

faq.q: Where do Houston candidates sit the API 653 exam?
faq.a: At a Prometric test centre, booked after API approves your application; Prometric lists centres in and around Houston. The exam is computer-based and takes about 7.5 hours including a tutorial and a 45-minute lunch break. During the open-book session the listed documents are on screen as PDFs, and you may not bring your own books, notes or papers.
